scenarios.objective: Separate the carrier’s pressure from a second attacker’s route.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. YOU are gold, returning toward the right net. The coach has assigned gold D1 to the navy puck carrier F1 for this rep. Navy F2 is moving through the other side of the middle; this movement is stated rather than animated.
cues: D1 has the carrier assignment for this rep.
F2 is a separate navy runner.

options.text: Identify who is pressuring the carrier.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a useful defensive relationship with F2 and the right net. Multiple recovery spots may work.
questions.explanation: The reference places YOU nearer the right net than F2 and close to the runner’s route. This illustrates a goal-side relationship; it does not prove interception timing or prescribe a fixed gap.

questions.prompt: Imagine YOU join D1 near F1, and both defenders stay close to the puck carrier. Which risk should you discuss before making that change?

options.text: F2 could have more room away from the two defenders
F1 could have more room away from the two defenders

questions.explanation: Putting both defenders near F1 can leave the separate runner F2 with less attention. Help may still be needed on F1, but communicate who will account for F2. Being close to the carrier does not prove that either defender wins the puck.

questions.prompt: What would make your backcheck different from simply skating toward the puck?
questions.explanation: Describe the teammate already applying pressure, the uncovered runner, and your route toward the defended net. A strong explanation also states what new cue would make you switch responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate on the backcheck?

options.text: D1 has F1; I am tracking F2 toward the right net
I am chasing the puck only
F2 does not receive

questions.prompt: Which two events can change your backcheck?

D1 loses contact with F1
The puck stays with F1

questions.prompt: Move YOU between F2 and the right net.
questions.explanation: This point places YOU on the defended net-side of F2 and keeps F1 visible; the recovery route remains conditional on F2’s movement.

questions.prompt: D1 calls for help after falling behind F1. How do you choose?
questions.explanation: Re-scan F1 and F2, then support the more dangerous reachable lane without losing sight of the second attacker.
